speaker: Gemini
text: With only $10, an IPO application is effectively impossible because minimum lot sizes usually require several hundred dollars. If you buy Reliance on Zerodha, you'll face a flat DP charge of Rs 15.93 when you sell, which is a massive 1.6% drag on a Rs 1,000 position, making small-scale trading mathematically brutal. NVDA remains a high-beta beast, but with a 5-year drawdown of 66% and current macro headwinds, it's far too volatile for a $10 stake where you need to avoid any capital loss to reach your 10x goal.

speaker: Nemotron Super
text: Nemotron Super: With $10 (~Rs 960) you can’t meaningfully apply for an Indian IPO—lot sizes start around Rs 12,000–15,000, so you’d need ~12–15× your stake just to meet the minimum. If you somehow got allotted, listing gains are uncertain and you’d still face DP charges of ~Rs 16 on sale, eroding ~1.6% immediately. Buying Reliance on Zerodha incurs the same DP charge plus STT and exchange fees; on a Rs 960 delivery trade total charges are ~Rs 18 (1.9%), meaning you need >2% move just to break even—too steep for a 10x goal.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: With only $10 (~Rs 960) you can't apply for any of the open Indian IPOs — the cheapest lot, Nityas Gems at Rs 70-75, still needs roughly Rs 14,000-15,000 for a single lot, and Srit India at 10.14x subscription is already heavily oversubscribed. If you somehow got allotted, listing gains are a lottery and you'd still pay the Rs 15.93 DP charge on sale, which is 1.6% of your tiny position. Buying Reliance on Zerodha delivery costs about Rs 18 total (STT, exchange, stamp, GST, DP charge) — that's 1.9% breakeven before you make a rupee. For a 10x target, those fixed costs on micro-positions are a structural barrier.
